name: CoWoS / advanced packaging
description_md: CoWoS-class 2.5D packaging is where the GPU die, HBM stacks, and interposer become a sellable AI accelerator — and it has been the hardest single constraint in the compute chain since 2023. Nvidia alone is reported to have booked ~60% of global 2026 CoWoS demand (~595k of ~1M wafers, ~515k from TSMC), leaving AMD, Broadcom, and the custom-ASIC programs to fight over the remainder. TSMC keeps raising capacity (including US expansion with Amkor in Arizona) and pushing overflow to ASE and Amkor, yet lead times still run 52-78 weeks. In August 2026 Foxconn's CEO — the world's largest AI-server assembler, downstream of everyone — named CoWoS packaging as the ceiling on AI-server growth into 2027: even with record earnings, assembly capacity is idle without packaged chips. Status basis: judged binding — the most explicitly rationed step in the chain, with the largest customer prepaying to hold ~60% of supply and lead times over a year.

controlled_by.share_note: Majority of global CoWoS-class capacity; sold out through 2027 per analysts (press_reported)
Largest OSAT; primary taker of TSMC CoWoS overflow — leading-edge packaging revenue >$3.5B 2026, targeting ≥$7.5B 2027 (company_claimed)
#2 OSAT; $7B Arizona campus (10-yr TSMC deal) adds US capacity from 2028 (company_pr)

dependents.dependency_md: ~60% of 2026 global CoWoS demand (~595k wafers, ~515k from TSMC) booked for Blackwell/Rubin; every GB/VR rack requires CoWoS-L. Packaging, not wafers, sets Nvidia's shipment ceiling.
MI-series accelerators use the same CoWoS-class flows; AMD's share of the ~40% non-Nvidia allocation caps its ability to convert AI demand into units.
Google TPU and other custom XPUs are CoWoS parts; hyperscaler custom-silicon roadmaps slip if allocation tightens.
Downstream assembler: CEO publicly named CoWoS as the 2027 ceiling on AI-server output — server assembly capacity exceeds packaged-chip supply.

substitutes_md: Partial only. TSMC's own SoIC/3D stacking and fan-out variants (CoWoS-R/L vs -S) trade off within the same constrained toolset. ASE/Amkor CoWoS-equivalent overflow lines relieve volume but require die-by-die qualification and stay a generation behind on the largest interposers. Samsung (I-Cube/H-Cube) and Intel (EMIB/Foveros) exist but essentially serve their own silicon; no AI flagship has ported. Co-packaged optics and panel-level packaging are 2027+ roadmap items, not current substitutes.
downcycle_md: This is where a demand fall would show up first and most violently: packaging capacity is chip-specific, the booking horizon is ~12-18 months, and much of the new ASE/Amkor/TSMC capacity was ordered against 2026-27 Nvidia forecasts. Nvidia's prepaid/reserved allocation functions like take-or-pay — TSMC keeps the cash — but OSAT overflow contracts are weaker (rolling POs), so ASE and Amkor would see utilization crack first, echoing the 2023 CoWoS whipsaw when TSMC briefly over-ordered tools. A glut would strand the record $10.5B ASE capex and turn 52-78-week lead times into discounting within two quarters; watch OSAT book-to-bill as the early indicator.

ASE record capex, raised twice in 2026, targeted at doubling leading-edge packaging revenue by 2027 — the scale of the overflow buildout.
